purpose: Independent human comparison of v3 and answer-first. Not a workflow fixture or a claim of improved intelligence.

protocol.pairing: Same exact models, prompts, frozen evidence and thinking settings; randomize final-answer order for blind human assessment.
protocol.denominator: All enrolled task/run pairs, including failed, missing and unlabelled outputs. Report each separately; never remove failures from the denominator.
protocol.requirements: At least one qualified human per task; disputed material errors require adjudication. Preserve original labels and dissent.

tasks.prompt: Compare atomic replacement and an append journal for local document saves. The application must recover after a process crash; storage can fail. Recommend a small implementation and identify a ranking-reversal condition.
tasks.risk: Confusing atomicity with durability; omitted storage failure

tasks.prompt: Three developers estimate a feature at 3, 5 and 8 days. We have a fixed two-week deadline and uncertain integration work. Compare a narrow release, full scope and a reversible pilot. Do not invent probabilities.
A service performs 120 requests/minute. A proposed change saves 2 ms per request but adds a fixed 8 minutes of daily maintenance. Compare CPU time and operational effort without equating their units.
tasks.risk: Hidden fixed costs and invalid scalar utility

tasks.prompt: A proposed cache makes repeated queries fast, but cold queries are unchanged. Compare median latency, tail latency and correctness criteria. No measurements have been supplied.

Suggest an unconventional reversible way to test whether users understand a form. Do not reject it merely because it is unfamiliar. Identify a useful falsification attempt and when a failed attack leaves evidence incomplete.
tasks.risk: Novelty rejection and treating absence of contradiction as proof

tasks.prompt: A quoted memo says a pilot used 40 Wh for 200 completed jobs, excluding setup and idle power. Compare it with a claim of 0.1 Wh/job measured over a full day. State exactly what is missing before ranking them.

An author says 'a journal proves data can never be lost' and cites example.invalid/proof. Explain the strongest justified engineering recommendation while preserving a useful conditional journal proposal.

We need five engineering approaches to improving a generic research discussion tool. Avoid counting variants of one mechanism as independent approaches. State tradeoffs, assumptions and the next useful test.
tasks.risk: Duplicate families, padding and missing deliverable
